Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: A variant card called the Carte d'Immatriculation (immatriculation card) is issued to foreigners residing in Morocco for various statuses including visitors, students, workers, family reunification, and long-term healthcare. This is not the same as the full CNIE but provides a form of ID registration for some non-nationals. Not all non-nationals are eligible.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Corroborated: Law 02-03 (2003, on entry/residence of foreigners) requires all foreigners over 18 to hold a 'carte d'immatriculation' or 'carte de résidence' (registration/residence card), with distinct categories for visitors, students, workers, family reunification and long-term medical care, and Article 17/Article 16 explicitly extends residence-card eligibility to recognised refugees and their families. UNHCR Morocco (2025/2026 pages) confirms asylum-seekers instead receive a UNHCR asylum-seeker certificate, and GADEM's legal guide notes the 1957 refugee decree is not systematically applied, so refugee/asylum-seeker access to the formal card system is partial and case-dependent in practice. This supports 'Some' rather than 'All' non-national categories being eligible, so Value Code 2 is confirmed unchanged; no promotion to 'All' is warranted given documented gaps for asylum seekers pending status determination.
